The defiantly disobedient break Allah's covenant, sever what He ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth, and they are the losers.
Those who die as disbelievers have the curse of Allah, the angels and all people upon them forever, with no lightening of the punishment and no reprieve.
Called to follow Allah's revelation, they follow their fathers instead; the disbelievers are like cattle that hear only calls and cries, deaf, dumb and blind.
The wealth and children of those who disbelieve will not avail them against Allah, and they are fuel for the Fire.
Those who disbelieve are told they will be overcome and gathered to Hell, a wretched resting place.
Allah does not guide those who disbelieve after believing and seeing clear signs; the curse of Allah, the angels and the people is on them, except those who repent.
Repentance is not accepted from those who increase in disbelief after belief, and those who die disbelievers could not ransom themselves with the earth's fill of gold.
Wealth and children will not help the disbelievers against Allah; what they spend in this life is like a frosty wind destroying a harvest.
Those hastening into disbelief will never harm Allah; they have no share in the Hereafter, and their extended time only increases their sin before a humiliating punishment.
Those who disbelieve, avert people from Allah's way and do wrong have strayed far; Allah will not forgive or guide them except to Hell forever.
Even the whole earth twice over would not ransom disbelievers from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection; they will wish to leave the Fire but never will.
They wait for angels, their Lord or signs, but when some signs come, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before or earned good through it.
They deserve punishment for barring people from al-Masjid al-Haram, whose guardians they are not; they spend wealth to avert from Allah's way and will be gathered to Hell.
They ask why no sign is sent down to him from his Lord; he is told to say the unseen belongs to Allah, so wait, and he waits with them.
Those on whom the word of the Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment.
If the punishment is delayed, they ask what detains it; on the Day it comes it will not be averted, and what they ridiculed will envelop them.
They urge evil before good, though similar punishments came before; they ask why no sign is sent, yet he is only a warner, and every people has a guide.
The deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ashes blown by the wind on a stormy day; they can keep nothing of what they earned.
Those who exchanged Allah's favor for disbelief settled their people in Hell; they set up equals to Allah to mislead; let them enjoy themselves, for their destination is the Fire.
Disbelievers may wish they had been Muslims; let them enjoy themselves; every nation has its term; they call the messenger mad and demand angels, sent down only with truth.
The disbelievers wait only for the angels or Allah's command, as those before them did, who wronged themselves and were overtaken by what they ridiculed.
Whoever willingly disbelieves after believing, unlike one forced while his heart stays firm in faith, faces Allah's wrath for preferring this world; their hearts are sealed and they are losers.
When the Quran is recited, a hidden partition and coverings keep deniers of the Hereafter from understanding; they turn away in aversion, saying he is a man affected by magic.
Given favor, the disbeliever turns away, and touched by evil he despairs; each acts in his own way, and your Lord knows best who is guided.
The greatest losers think they do well while their efforts are lost; they disbelieved in their Lord's verses and meeting Him, and mocked His signs, so their recompense is Hell.
They demand a sign though earlier scriptures are evidence; had they been destroyed first they would have asked for a messenger; each waits, and they will know who is guided.
Disbelievers mock the Prophet and impatiently ask when the promise will come; the Fire will reach them suddenly, as earlier mockers of messengers were overwhelmed by what they ridiculed.
Those who disbelieve and bar people from Allah's way and from al-Masjid al-Haram, equal for resident and visitor, will taste painful punishment, as will anyone intending wrongdoing there.
They urge the Prophet to hasten the punishment, but Allah never fails His promise, a day with Him is like a thousand years, and He seized many cities after respite.
No soul is burdened beyond its capacity and a truthful record is kept, yet disbelievers' hearts are confused, and their affluent, once seized by punishment, cry for help in vain.
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter deviate from the path; even shown mercy they would persist, suffering did not humble them, and severe punishment will bring despair.
The deeds of disbelievers are like a mirage that proves to be nothing, or like layered darkness in a deep sea; whoever Allah gives no light has no light.
Disbelievers cannot cause Allah failure on the earth, and their refuge will be the Fire.
They ridicule the Prophet as nearly misleading them from their gods; whoever takes his own desire as a god is like livestock, or even further astray.
Told to prostrate to the Most Merciful, they ask what the Most Merciful is, and it increases them in aversion.
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter find their deeds made pleasing so they wander blindly, and they will have the worst punishment and be the greatest losers.
The Prophet tells people to see the end of the criminals, is told not to grieve over their plots, and answers those demanding the promise that some may be close.
The disbelievers of Quraysh offer to carry believers' sins if followed, but they lie; they will carry their own burdens and more, and be questioned on the Day of Resurrection.
They urge the punishment on, but it will come suddenly at its appointed term, and Hell will encompass the disbelievers, covering them from above and below.
Allah made Makkah a safe sanctuary while people around are taken away, yet they believe falsehood and deny His favor; none is more unjust than one who lies about Allah.
Disbelievers ask when the conquest will be; then their belief will not benefit them nor will they be reprieved, so the Prophet is to turn away and wait.
Terrified and seized with no escape, disbelievers will then claim belief though they disbelieved before, and will be barred from what they desire, as their kind were before.
Allah made people successors on earth, and whoever disbelieves bears his own disbelief, which only increases disbelievers in their Lord's hatred and in loss.
Disbelievers turn from every sign, answer the call to spend by asking why feed those Allah could feed, and ask when the promise comes; one blast will seize them disputing.
Quraysh used to say that with a message like the former peoples' they would be Allah's chosen servants, yet they disbelieved in it and will come to know.
By the Quran with its reminder, the disbelievers are in pride and dissension, though many generations before them were destroyed, crying out when there was no escape.
These disbelievers await only a single blast that will not be delayed, yet ask their Lord to hasten their share before the Day of Account.
Disbelievers are told Allah's hatred of them exceeded their hatred of themselves; they confess their sins and ask for a way out, having disbelieved when Allah was called upon alone.
By the heaven with pathways, people differ in speech; the heedless falsifiers deluded from the Quran ask when the Day of Recompense is, and will be tormented over the Fire.
The disbelievers of Quraysh are asked if they are better than earlier peoples or immune by scripture; their assembly will be defeated and flee, and the Hour is their appointment.
Those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are abased like those before them, and on the Day Allah resurrects them He will inform them of what they did.
The Prophet is told to strive against the disbelievers and hypocrites and be harsh with them; their refuge is Hell.
Do not obey the deniers or the habitual swearer, scorner and gossip, proud of wealth and children, who calls Allah's verses legends; he will be branded on the snout.
Disbelievers crowding around the Prophet hoping for Paradise were created from what they know; Allah can replace them, so leave them until they rush from the graves on their Day.
Disbelievers flee from the reminder like alarmed donkeys from a lion, each wanting scriptures of his own, for they do not fear the Hereafter.
The disbeliever neither believed nor prayed, but denied, turned away and went to his people swaggering; woe to him, and woe.
The criminals may eat and enjoy briefly; they refuse to bow when told, and are asked in what statement after the Quran they will believe.
The record of the wicked is in sijjeen; woe to those who deny the Day of Recompense and call Allah's verses legends; their hearts are stained, and they will burn.
By the twilight, night and full moon, people will pass from state to state; yet disbelievers do not believe or prostrate at the Quran, and face punishment, unlike righteous believers.
